methodology: Read SOP_VISUAL_ONLY.md §3/§4 (direction authority) and the package docs (visual-direction.md, color-system.md, surface-system.md, button-system.md, data-display-system.md) against the rendered gallery code (component-gallery.html/.css/.js, design-tokens.css).
Offline render via agent-browser (file:// URL, no network — console clean, zero remote resources per captures/console-messages.txt and network-remote-resources.txt).

Live computed-style probes: real keyboard focus on inputs and buttons (Tab navigation), measured heights of chips/segmented buttons at 100% and 200% root font size, menu/nav/tag/snackbar resolved colors.

Independent WCAG 2.1 contrast recomputation of 50 rendered pairs (sub4-visual-critique.py, results in contrast-grayscale-results.json) — verifies every claim in color-system.md and extends to focus-ring/border/tint non-text pairs the package did not compute.
Grayscale (relative-luminance) confusability analysis of all state-bearing colors and tint surfaces.
A11y snapshot review at 320/360/390/430 × LTR/RTL (captures/current-*.txt) plus behavior captures (loading guard, sheet/dialog/snackbar, undo, completion reset).
Source-pack cross-check: rendered-reference/*.html and reference-components for inheritance verification of contested roles (chip-active, badge-ready, jar tile, FAB, nav active).

grayscale_risks: accent.50 (Ready tag tint) vs operational.50 (Moved tag tint): 1.04:1 — two unrelated semantic statuses render as the same pale pill in grayscale (and are within a few RGB points in color); icons/text are the only differentiators.

accent.700 (secondary pressed) vs operational.600 (Transfer fill): 1.08:1; accent.600 vs operational.600: 1.38:1 — a pressed state of one action and a semantic quick-action of another family are near-identical dark cool fills.

positive.500 (Accept) vs negative.500 (Delete record): 1.05:1 and primary.700 vs negative.500: 1.16:1 — filled buttons of different variants converge in grayscale; different labels save them (never color-alone is respected via text).

Tints vs recessed surfaces: positive.50/recessed 1.01:1, primary.100/recessed 1.07:1, accent.50/gold.50 1.05:1 — all tint surfaces collapse onto the ivory layer in grayscale; selection/status must not rely on tint alone (chips do not — they use fill; nav does not — icon fill-switch; tags rely on text+icon where present).
Skeleton blocks at 1.10:1 vs canvas become static and near-invisible under prefers-reduced-motion (pulse is the only strengthening cue).
Pressed deltas survive grayscale well: primary 700→800 (ΔL 0.049 + 0.97 scale) and accent 600→700 (ΔL 0.068) are perceivable; loading is distinguished from pressed by spinner + label, not color.

findings.evidence: component-gallery.css:194 `.input:focus { border-color: var(--color-accent-500); outline: none; }` overrides design-tokens.css:252 `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent-600) }` (specificity 0,2,0 > 0,1,0). Live verification (Tab focus, :focus-visible=true): #f-name computed `outline: 3px none`, border settles to rgb(7,159,160) after the 200ms transition; inputs family head (component-gallery.html:170) claims 'focus shifts the border and adds the system ring'; button-system.md Focused contract: '2px accent.600 ring, 2px offset'.
findings.criterion: Mission: 'focus indication is not color-only-subtle'; Repair H 'focus visible'; package's own unified-ring contract.
findings.finding: Real keyboard focus on every text input, textarea and amount field shows NO system ring — the only cue is a 1px border recoloring (1.25:1 → 3.24:1) that fades in over 200ms. The static 'Focused' demo (.is-focused) shows a ring, so the gallery misrepresents actual behavior. This is the exact color-only-subtle failure mode named in the mission.
findings.recommendation: Remove `outline: none` from `.input:focus` and let the global :focus-visible ring apply (inputs already get outline-offset:0 + accent.500 border from design-tokens.css:257-262). Keep the border shift as the secondary cue.

findings.evidence: Live probe: `.btn-secondary` focused → `outline: 2px solid rgb(5,123,124)` on `background: rgb(5,123,124)` — 1.00:1. Computed: accent.600 vs primary.700 = 1.20:1. Ring passes vs all four surfaces (canvas 4.83, surface 5.08, recessed 4.38, ink 3.27) only because of the 2px offset gap.
findings.criterion: WCAG 1.4.11 / 2.4.11 — focus indicator must be distinguishable from the component itself; Repair H 'focus visibility'.
findings.finding: The unified focus ring is invisible-as-distinct on the accent.600 secondary button (identical color to its own fill) and reads as a dark halo on primary.700 fills. A single flat ring color mathematically cannot pass 3:1 against both light surfaces and the two dark fills (accent.200 passes vs fills 3.06/3.69 but fails vs canvas 1.57).
findings.recommendation: Two documented options within existing tokens: (a) declare the 2px offset gap an intentional part of the indicator and increase ring to 3px for filled variants; (b) for dark filled buttons only, switch to an inset ring `outline: 2px solid var(--color-surface); outline-offset: -2px` (white = 5.08:1 on both accent.600 and primary.700, no new color). Decide and document; do not leave the accent-on-accent case as-is.

findings.evidence: current-ltr-320.txt:136-140 `button "All" [ref=e81]` (no [pressed]); :158-160 `button "Day"`; :264-267 nav `button "Home"` — no state annotations. component-gallery.js:69-77, 108-117, 308-316 toggle only the `on` class; component-gallery.html:250, 283-290, 446-461 have no aria-pressed/aria-selected/aria-current.
findings.criterion: WCAG 4.1.2 (name/role/value); 'never color alone' must include programmatic state.
findings.finding: Selection state of filter chips, both segmented variants, and the bottom nav is visual-only — screen-reader users receive no selected/active information. The dropdown menu does expose aria-selected, so the system is internally inconsistent.
findings.recommendation: Chips + segmented: aria-pressed="true/false" (or radiogroup/tablist roles with aria-checked/aria-selected); bottom nav: aria-current="page" on the active item. Pure JS/HTML addition, zero visual change.

findings.evidence: Computed: accent.50 #E3F5F5 (Ready) vs operational.50 #E8EEF3 (Moved) = 1.04:1; accent.600 vs operational.600 = 1.38:1. Gallery: tag-ready and menu option.on use identical accent.50/600 pairings (component-gallery.css:237, 275). Source inheritance: source-tokens status.ready #079FA0 (tailwind.config.source.js via rendered-reference/accounting-mobile-components.html:53).
findings.criterion: Repair B: 'no multiple near-identical terracotta/teal shades for unrelated meanings'; 'operational statuses must stay separate from button states and filters'.
findings.finding: The teal family simultaneously codes: secondary action (600 fill), ghost action (600 text), focus (600 ring / 500 border), dropdown selection (50/600), and the 'Ready' status (50/600). Ready vs Moved — two different semantic statuses — are near-identical pale pills in grayscale and extremely close in color. The conflation is inherited, but the gallery adds menu-selection to the same tokens, deepening it.
findings.recommendation: Within the no-new-colors constraint: (1) make the leading icon mandatory on every status tag (Ready=clock/check, Moved=bank) and keep text distinct — structure carries the separation (Repair B's prescribed mechanism); (2) document that accent.50/600 is a dual-role token (status+selection) and consider moving menu selection to a primary.700-check-on-accent.50 hybrid or the documented check glyph in accent.600; (3) never render Ready and Moved pills adjacent without icons.

findings.evidence: computed-structure.txt: `"textModes":["normal","large"]`; component-gallery.html:77-80 (A / A+ only); large = 17px root ≈ 106%. Live probe at 32px root (200%): buttons 96px, chips 72px (after transition), labels 26px — the rem architecture scales correctly but is undemonstrated.
findings.criterion: Repair H: '100/130/200% text scale'.
findings.finding: The gallery demonstrates only 100% and ~106% text scale. The 130% and 200% checkpoints required by the repair contract are absent, so clipping/wrapping behavior of long labels at 200% is unverified in the deliverable (though spot-probes suggest it works).
findings.recommendation: Extend the Text control to 100/130/200 (root 16/20.8/32px) and add a long-label sample (Arabic + Latin) per family; record 200% screenshots as evidence.

findings.evidence: component-gallery.html:401 is the only Arabic string (`تحويل داخلي`, short); .row-title is nowrap+ellipsis (component-gallery.css:384-388; computed-structure.txt `rowTitleWhiteSpace: nowrap`); data-display-system.md: 'long names use line-clamp, never mid-word truncation'; SOP §6: 'Do not use fixed heights that clip Arabic'.
findings.criterion: Repair H: 'long Arabic labels'; direction: 'readable Arabic'.
findings.finding: No long-Arabic-label demonstration exists anywhere in the gallery — no long Arabic button, chip, field label, sheet row, or row title; the single Arabic title is short and the row truncation strategy is single-line ellipsis, not the documented line-clamp, so Arabic meaning is destroyed rather than wrapped.
findings.recommendation: Add a row with a long Arabic title (2-line clamp), an Arabic long-label button, and an Arabic field label; switch .row-title to -webkit-line-clamp:2 (direction-compliant, existing behavior).

findings.evidence: component-gallery.css:245 inline SVG check stroke '%23079FA0' (accent.500) on .menu button.on background accent.50 #E3F5F5 (css:237) — computed 2.88:1 < 3.0.
findings.criterion: WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast; the check is the menu's non-color selection cue.
findings.finding: The dropdown's selected-option check mark — the very element that makes selection not-color-only — fails non-text contrast against its own tint.
findings.recommendation: Stroke the check with accent.600 #057B7C (4.51:1 on accent.50) — one-character change in the data-URI, existing ramp step.

findings.evidence: component-gallery.html:305-320 — three badge rows render 10 colored pills at once (progress/ready/closed + 4 semantic + 3 text-only); family head line 300 claims 'Every pairing carries an icon or dot so state never rides on color alone' but the third row (Paid/Cancelled/Returned) is text-only; the chips section (lines 260-266) shows 5 of 7 tags without icons.
findings.criterion: Repair B: 'no permanent row of colored pills exposing every status; when statuses are shown, use semantic roles + text + iconography + structure together'.
findings.finding: The Badges family demonstrates the exact anti-pattern Repair B prohibits — a static wall of every status pill at equal weight — and contradicts its own caption: icon coverage is inconsistent across the two presentations of the same tag set.
findings.recommendation: Restructure the Badges frame: (1) one in-context composition (a row list or card) using at most two semantic families with icons+text, per the docs' own restraint rule; (2) a compact labeled catalog (smaller, with mandatory icon/dot on every pill); (3) move the full swatch matrix to the evidence panel. Make the leading icon mandatory for all status tags in both sections.

findings.evidence: Live measurement: .segctl button height 40px (css:297 `min-height: 40px` hardcoded px); .segctl-lines button 40.8px (css:306 padding 10px 0); at 32px root the seg button stayed 46px (content-driven) proving the px hardcode. SOP §6 target 44×44; button-system.md claims 'Everything is rem-based'.
findings.criterion: SOP §6 touch target 44px; Repair H non-color/geometry.
findings.finding: Segmented control buttons and underline tabs fall below the 44px touch-target minimum and use hardcoded px that contradict the rem-scaling contract (chips correctly use the 36+8 pad trick = 44px hit area; buttons/inputs 48px).
findings.recommendation: min-height: var(--touch-target) (2.75rem = 44px) on both segmented variants; replace px paddings with rem equivalents.

findings.evidence: Buttons: disabled fill + white (css:151-154, 2.11:1). Chips: recessed fill + disabled text (css:267, 1.82:1). Inputs: recessed fill + disabled text (css:197). Docs specify only the button recipe (SOP §7.1; button-system.md).
findings.criterion: Coherence: one disabled grammar.
findings.finding: Three different disabled recipes coexist — a filled grey-out (buttons), a tinted grey-out with grey text (chips), and a recessed field with grey text (inputs). All are WCAG-exempt, but the system reads as three systems.
findings.recommendation: Standardize on the SOP button recipe for all filled controls, and recessed+disabled-text for all outline/field controls; document both as the two sanctioned disabled forms.

findings.evidence: Chips selected = primary.700 fill (css:263-266, documented data-display-system.md:29); segmented thumb primary.700 (css:290); nav active primary.100/700 (css:454-456); menu selection = accent.50/600 (css:237, documented color-system.md:10 'dropdown selection').
findings.criterion: visual-direction.md: 'Selected chips, segmented thumbs, active navigation pills, and focused fields all use the same recognizable grammar'.
findings.finding: The selection grammar is split across two hues: compact pill controls select in terracotta, the dropdown selects in teal — and the teal selection tokens are identical to the Ready status tag. Both halves are documented, so this is an inherited divergence rather than an error, but a single screen mixing a selected chip with a selected menu row shows two 'selected' looks.
findings.recommendation: Optional normalization: keep terracotta for all filled-selection states (chips/segments/nav) and teal strictly for focus + check-mark selection glyphs, with the check recolored to make the distinction visible; or accept and document the split explicitly in visual-direction.md.

findings.evidence: component-gallery.html:347 + css:355 tile-chip-primary (primary.100 bg, primary.700 icon) on the 'Reserved' tile; inherited from accounting-mockup.html:121-128 ('حق المحل' jar chip); color-system.md Prohibition 5: 'Never use terracotta for amounts or data meaning'.
findings.criterion: Terracotta = identity chrome only.
findings.finding: Terracotta carries quasi-semantic data meaning on the Reserved tile (held funds — an operational concept) next to a positive-green 'Free' tile, mixing identity color into the semantic layer of one composition.
findings.recommendation: Switch the Reserved tile-chip to operational.50 + operational.600 (existing steps) so both tiles in the featured card are semantic and terracotta stays identity-only; note the deviation from the inherited source composition in the decision log.

findings.evidence: Grep: --color-primary-500 defined (design-tokens.css:21) but zero uses in component-gallery.css; HTML head meta theme-color #CC785C only. Source: FAB bg-primary #CC785C (accounting-mockup.html:301), chip-active #CC785C, nav active #CC785C. self-critique.md item 1 acknowledges the button judgment (D-01).
findings.criterion: Direction: 'warm Terracotta identity'; mission key value: primary.500 #CC785C identity.
findings.finding: The documented identity color #CC785C never renders inside any composition — every visible terracotta is 700/800/100/200. The corrections are measured and SOP-sanctioned, but the net identity is deep brown-terracotta, visibly heavier than the source look. [Judgment, labeled: the system remains warm and coherent; this is a character shift, not a defect.]
findings.recommendation: Optional, within the SOP's non-text allowance: restore primary.500 for one non-text identity moment — the FAB fill (white 24px icon = 3.28:1, passes 1.4.11 non-text) or selected glyph accents — so the documented identity hue exists in the rendered system; keep 700 for all text-bearing fills. Alternatively re-describe primary.700 as 'the rendered identity step' in visual-direction.md to close the doc-rendered gap.

findings.evidence: Computed accent.600 vs primary.700 = 1.20:1 (ring-to-fill adjacency); ring vs canvas 4.83:1, vs recessed 4.38:1, vs ink 3.27:1 (all pass).
findings.criterion: WCAG 1.4.11 adjacent-color contrast for the focus indicator.
findings.finding: On primary.700 fills the teal ring is perceptually a dark halo rather than a distinct colored ring; it technically passes because the 2px offset gap makes the surrounding surface the adjacent color on both ring edges.
findings.recommendation: Fold into the S4-02 decision (gap-as-indicator documentation or inset white ring for dark fills).

findings.evidence: component-gallery.css:384-388 (.row-title nowrap/ellipsis); computed-structure.txt confirms; data-display-system.md:39 'long names use line-clamp, never mid-word truncation'.
findings.criterion: Direction: readable Arabic and long labels preserve meaning.
findings.finding: Row titles use single-line ellipsis where the docs mandate line-clamp; long titles (the gallery's own demo title) lose most of their content in one line.
findings.recommendation: -webkit-line-clamp: 2 on .row-title (with the S4-06 long-Arabic sample as proof).

findings.evidence: component-gallery.js:243-271 — loading changes label to 'Saving' with no aria-live/aria-busy on the button; menu markup (component-gallery.html:199-204) uses button[role=option] with no arrow-key handling; behavior-loading-snapshot.txt shows the label/disabled change works visually.
findings.criterion: WCAG 4.1.2/ARIA APG listbox pattern; state changes perceivable to AT.
findings.finding: Programmatic announce gaps: loading-state label change is silent to AT; the listbox role implies arrow-key navigation that is not implemented; skeleton (role=status) and snackbar (role=status) are correctly announced, so coverage is uneven.
findings.recommendation: Add aria-busy="true" (and optionally a visually-hidden live region) on the loading button; either implement arrow-key handling for the menu or downgrade to a plain button + aria-expanded menu pattern.

findings.evidence: Navigation frame (component-gallery.html:425-467): FAB primary.700 + active nav primary.100/700 + action-bar 'Confirm summary' primary.700 in one .screen; Buttons Variants frame (119-133) stacks 5+ filled buttons at equal weight; pair-row shows Accept (positive.500) + Transfer (operational.600) as equal filled pair. visual-direction.md: 'Exactly one filled identity action leads each viewport'. [Judgment, labeled.]
findings.criterion: SOP §10: 'Do not present several filled buttons with equal visual weight in one viewport'.
findings.finding: Catalog frames necessarily violate the one-filled rule, and the Navigation demo compounds FAB + nav + action bar in one screen. Acceptable as a library, but the gallery lacks a single 'correct hierarchy' composition that demonstrates the rule it preaches — the strongest hierarchy demo currently contradicts it.
findings.recommendation: Add one realistic screen composition (e.g., a records list screen) with exactly one filled primary, outline secondary, ghost tertiary — the reference implementation of the hierarchy rule; split the Navigation frame into top-bar/nav and action-bar sub-frames.

findings.evidence: Computed: recessed #F0EEE6 vs canvas #FAF9F5 = 1.10:1 (vs surface 1.17:1); design-tokens.css:275-282 kills animation under prefers-reduced-motion; component-gallery.html:530-537 skeleton sits directly on the canvas .screen; role=status carries the announcement.
findings.criterion: Mission: non-color state cues everywhere; loading must be visible without motion.
findings.finding: Skeleton placeholders are nearly invisible on canvas/surface, and their only strengthening cue (pulse) is removed under reduced motion — leaving a static, almost-unseeable loading indication for low-vision users.
findings.recommendation: Base skeletons on divider #DAD5C8 (existing neutral, ~1.47:1) or add a 1px border-soft edge; keep shapes promising the real layout (already good: title/line/card/row shapes).

findings.evidence: component-gallery.css:167 `.iconbtn-primary { box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm) }` in the resting top bar; design-tokens.css:181 documents shadow-sm for the segmented thumb; surface-system.md: 'Top bar: canvas-colored at rest' (flat).
findings.criterion: Surface discipline: no shadow on flat chrome.
findings.finding: A resting top-bar icon button carries a shadow reserved for the segmented thumb, contradicting the flat-at-rest chrome contract.
findings.recommendation: Remove box-shadow from .iconbtn-primary (or apply only on :active).

findings.evidence: component-gallery.css:597 `.ev-ramp span::after { font-size: 10px }` in the evidence panel.
findings.criterion: 12px floor (SOP §8; visual-direction.md 'never smaller than 12px').
findings.finding: Evidence-panel ramp labels render at 10px — below the documented floor. It is documentation chrome, but the gallery should model its own rule everywhere it draws text.
findings.recommendation: Raise to var(--text-caption-size) (12px) or make the labels tooltips-only.

findings.evidence: component-gallery.css:437 bottomnav padding hardcodes 16px bottom (env(safe-area-inset-bottom) utilities exist in design-tokens.css:248 but unused); css:260 `.chip { transition: all ... }` — live measurement showed chips animating min-height over 200ms on text-size change.
findings.criterion: Safe-area behavior (SOP §11); motion discipline (targeted properties).
findings.finding: Safe-area utilities are defined but not wired into the nav demo; `transition: all` on chips animates layout properties (min-height/padding) — a motion-discipline smell that also lags large-text resizing.
findings.recommendation: Add safe-area padding to bottomnav/actionbar demos; scope chip transition to background-color/color/border-color/transform.

findings.evidence: current-ltr-320.txt:255-259 — heading 'Records' [level=2] appears twice (two topbar demos) inside the Navigation family which itself has an h2; component-gallery.html:429-441.
findings.criterion: Heading hierarchy sanity for AT navigation.
findings.finding: Duplicate h2 'Records' (plus the family h2) pollutes the heading outline with repeated demo chrome.
findings.recommendation: Mark the second top-bar demo's title aria-hidden or demote both demo titles to h3/h4.

findings.evidence: component-gallery.html:138-162 state strip (Default / Pressed—hold / Focused / Disabled / Loading—tap / Quiet completion) with .state-tag labels; css:135/157/158 pressed=800+scale, loading=800+spinner+label, completion=positive.50+check+label; grayscale ladder 700=0.12 / 800=0.073 / disabled=0.45 / complete-tint=0.86.
findings.criterion: Repair A: six button states shown together as STATES of one button.
findings.finding: POSITIVE FINDING — Repair A is fully satisfied: the six states are presented as one labeled strip of the same button, each distinguished by structure (scale, spinner, check icon, label text) as well as color; all six remain pairwise distinguishable in grayscale. This pattern should be protected during repair.
findings.recommendation: Keep as-is; reuse the labeled-state-strip pattern for inputs and chips in the repair.

top_5: S4-01 (blocker): real keyboard focus shows no ring on any input — `.input:focus { outline: none }` kills the unified ring; restore it (one-line CSS fix).
S4-03: chip/segmented/nav selection is visual-only — add aria-pressed / aria-selected / aria-current so 'never color alone' includes programmatic state.

S4-02/S4-14: the accent.600 focus ring is 1.00:1 on the secondary button's own fill and 1.20:1 on primary fills — decide and document a dark-fill ring strategy (offset-gap doctrine or inset white ring) using existing tokens only.

S4-08/S4-04 (Repair B): the Badges frame is a wall of 10 colored pills with inconsistent icon coverage, and Ready (accent.50) vs Moved (operational.50) tints are 1.04:1 apart — restructure badges in-context with mandatory icons and document the teal dual-role.
S4-05/S4-06 (Repair H): add 130%/200% text-scale steps and long-Arabic-label samples with line-clamp (currently only a short Arabic string and normal/large text modes exist).
